rubrics.criterion: The record-time per-cpu kernel writer manipulation (descriptor/array construction, per-cpu trace-pipe and output-file opening, and the end-of-session drain/close/release) is performed by the kernel tracing module's own functions again, not by helpers defined in the record command.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's core drifted cluster is the record command doing the kernel module's writer-internal work; the resolution is measured by where that manipulation actually executes after the patch, in whatever function layout the solver chooses.

rubrics.criterion: Kernel reader construction (parser init, kernel-cpu directory scan, rstack list setup) and reader teardown (per-cpu release and buffer frees) are owned and executed by the kernel tracing module again, with the data-file layer calling into it.
rubrics.rationale: The replay-side cluster moved whole reader lifecycle functions into the data-file layer; the resolution is the ownership returning to the module that defines the reader struct, independent of which public entry points the solver keeps.

rubrics.criterion: The graph command resolves user-supplied function names by going through the symbol module's by-name lookup rather than a command-local probe of symbol-table internals.
rubrics.rationale: The duplicated probe is one of this instance's three clusters; the outcome is that the command uses the symbol module again, however the call is shaped.

rubrics.criterion: The kernel module's writer lifecycle entry points are complete implementations again: no part of the per-cpu setup/open/cleanup is still performed by command-side helpers running alongside them, and no withered fragment of those steps remains in the module.
rubrics.rationale: In this instance the drift fragmented the lifecycle (owner functions kept only halves). A sound repair reintegrates the logic; a partial one that leaves both a module function and a command helper doing pieces of the same lifecycle step does not resolve the relation.

rubrics.criterion: Call sites in the record command and the data-file layer hand the kernel module the kernel writer/reader state itself, rather than threading command-layer or data-file-layer context structs through the kernel module's logic.
rubrics.rationale: The drifted helpers in this instance take the record command's writer-bundle type and the graph collector type; a repair that keeps the module's signature parameterized by consumer-layer structs simply relocates the coupling. This is assessed on the final call shape between the consumers and the owning module.

rubrics.criterion: The kernel module's public header no longer declares the kernel-header loader that was exposed only so the data-file layer could construct the reader.
rubrics.rationale: This instance contains a supporting public-header exposure whose only purpose was to make the displaced reader construction compile. Leaving it (or an equivalent re-exposure) behind after the construction returns to the module is an unmodeled leftover of the drift.

rubrics.criterion: The kernel-cpu directory scan helpers (the filter/sort callbacks the reader construction passes to the directory scan) live in the same module as the reader construction that uses them.
rubrics.rationale: The scan callbacks traveled with the displaced construction in this instance; after repair they must not remain stranded in the data-file layer where nothing else uses them, nor be duplicated in two modules.

rubrics.criterion: No dead or duplicated copies of the displaced logic remain in the command or data-file layers (e.g., the record command's kernel writer helpers or the graph command's by-name probe and its comparator surviving as unused or parallel code).
rubrics.rationale: A repair that adds owner-side implementations but leaves the drifted copies in place keeps the duplication this instance asks to clean up.

rubrics.criterion: No include directives that were added only to support the displaced logic remain in the consumer files (tracing-filesystem helpers included by the record command; the directory-scan and stdlib includes pulled into the data-file layer for the moved reader code).
rubrics.rationale: This instance's drift required consumer files to pull in headers their remaining code does not otherwise need; leaving them behind is a concrete leftover that this specific repair should clear.

rubrics.criterion: The repair leaves the kernel module's linkage consistent with actual callers: a function still called from other translation units is declared through the kernel module's public header rather than left with file-local linkage only, and a function only the module itself calls is not left exported through the public header.
rubrics.rationale: The defining drift reshuffled static/public linkage of kernel module functions in both directions (the loader exposure, the still-public reader functions with their in-module test callers); the repaired linkage should match actual use rather than one of these two failure directions.

rubrics.criterion: The record command's kernel tracing availability handling is externally unchanged: a setup or start failure still disables kernel tracing for the session and emits the same warnings the pre-repair tree emits.
rubrics.rationale: The drifted lifecycle fragments sit inside these enable/disable decisions in this instance; a careless reintegration can drop or duplicate the disablement path, which silent unit coverage would not catch because kernel tracing needs a live tracer.

rubrics.criterion: The kernel tracing session teardown still leaves the same end state as before the repair: remaining trace data is still drained before close, the recorded kernel data files are still saved, and the tracefs configuration is still restored.
rubrics.rationale: This instance split the teardown into a consumer-side drain/close piece and an owner-side save/reset piece; the observable end state of a kernel-traced session is the invariant that must survive any reintegration.

rubrics.criterion: The cleanup does not remove or break the symbol module's name-keyed lookup that other in-tree consumers still use, including the tracing runtime's post-record symbol resolution.
rubrics.rationale: Because this instance duplicates a live API rather than replacing it, an overzealous cleanup could delete the owner-side probe along with the copy and break callers outside the command layer, which the unit suite alone does not exercise.

rubrics.criterion: The repaired failure paths of the kernel writer lifecycle do not leak or double-release per-cpu state (what gets opened on error is closed exactly once, and allocations are freed on the same paths as before the repair).
rubrics.rationale: The drifted open-step in this instance carried only part of the original error cleanup; reintegrating the fragments is exactly where a solution can drop, duplicate or reorder the cleanup of per-cpu descriptors.
